name: XDKNet 2.5.14
body:
Android TV 2.5.14. Works with XDKNet server plugin 2.1.0.13 (Emby 2.0.5.13); no plugin update is needed.

TVs on 2.4.10 or later offer this update on their own. On 2.4.9, use
Settings > About > Check for updates. Anything older has to install it once
by hand, from the `XDKNet_AndroidTV.apk` below.

This release is for everyone. Nothing in it needs admin rights.

## Audio and subtitles

- **One Audio & Subtitles panel.** Press Up from the seek bar, or the
  captions or audio button on your remote, to open it. Back closes the panel,
  not the film.
- **Tracks are named by their language**, such as "English" or
  "Spanish (Forced)", with the technical details in small print.
- With Settings > Clock set to "Always", the time now shows in the player
  too.

## Playback fixes

- Leaving the player while a stream was restarting could wipe your resume
  point. It is kept now.
- After the TV had been in the background, a film could come back in its
  default version instead of the one you picked. It keeps your version now.
- Skipping the credits of a film or a show's last episode now marks it as
  watched, so it leaves Continue Watching.
- "Still watching?" now also appears when the Next Up card is turned off,
  and no longer asks at the end of a series when nothing comes next.
- A show's logo no longer overlaps the episode line at the top of the
  player.

## Exit

- **Exit at Home now closes the app completely.** Playback stops and is
  reported to the server first, and the next launch starts fresh. If a
  download is still running in the app itself, the Exit prompt says so,
  since it will have to start over.

## Browsing

- If the server can't be reached, pages say so in plain words with a Retry
  button instead of showing error codes, and Home shows a small note until
  the server is back.
- If your sign-in stops working while the app is open (a password change,
  or the device was removed on the server), the app takes you back to
  sign-in instead of failing on every screen.
- Library grids update watched ticks, progress and favourites straight
  away, and changing a filter or sort quickly no longer mixes in titles
  from the old one.
- A show with one new episode in Latest no longer takes that episode's
  watched mark or progress bar.
- Home rows no longer mix up when a row is refreshed while more of it is
  loading.
- Search finds films, shows and episodes even when many songs or episodes
  match the same word, and library search finds titles by their name as
  written.
- Watched and favourite marks always go to the title's own server when
  more than one server is signed in.
- Times under a minute show in seconds, such as "Resume from 6s", instead
  of "0m".

## Safer connections

- **The app checks your server's certificate** on https addresses, unless
  you turned on Settings > Account & Security > Allow self-signed
  certificates. If a server's certificate is refused, sign-in and the server
  list say so and offer that setting, and the app never quietly switches to
  plain http instead.
- Sign-in tokens moved out of the app's plain settings file into the
  system's secure storage. You stay signed in through the update.
- Android backups leave out sign-ins, download records and the device id.
- Downloads always stay inside the downloads folder, whatever names the
  server sends.
- Only the system and media apps can browse your library through the app's
  media service.
- Switching accounts moves push notifications to the account you switched to.

## Home address

- Fewer checks in the background, nothing hangs when a phone leaves Wi-Fi,
  and players wait for the home address to be checked before starting a
  stream there.
- An https home address with its own certificate is still accepted.
